privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.updated: Last updated 31 October 2026 (photos, secret admirer, games and community added)
privacy.intro: Dearlly is a love-letter post office. You trust us with words meant for one person, so we collect as little as we can, keep it locked, and never sell it. This notice explains what we keep, why, and how to have it removed, in line with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

sections.heading: What we keep about you
paragraphs: When you create an account:
items: Your email address, so you can log in and we can send you login codes.
Your username and the display name you choose.
Your password, if you set one. We only keep a scrambled version that can't be turned back into the password.
That you confirmed you're 18 or older, and when.
If you use "Continue with Google": your Google account ID and email. We never see your Google password.

sections.heading: Your letters
paragraphs: We keep what you write so the person you send it to can open it: the names, the message, the date it opens, and their reply. We also keep whether and when it was opened, so you can see "Opened".
We don't read your letters. The only time someone at Dearlly looks at one is when it is reported, to decide whether to take it down.

If you send a letter as a secret admirer, the person you send it to doesn't see your name until you reveal it, but Dearlly always keeps a record of who sent it, so a report or a block can be acted on.
Unsent drafts stay on your own phone or computer until you seal them. Downloads (pictures and PDFs) are made on your device; nothing is sent to us.

sections.heading: Photos
paragraphs: If you add a photo to a letter, we save a fresh copy of it: location and other hidden details from your phone are removed.
Before anyone sees it, a program on our own server checks it for nudity or sexual content. Photos it flags are refused and never stored. No photo is sent to another company for this check.
Photos are kept in private storage and shown only through links that expire within two hours. A photo you add but never send is deleted after a day; your photos are deleted with your account.

sections.heading: Games
paragraphs: When you play a game, your answers and the in-game chat are only shown to the two players. They're kept on our server while you play and deleted an hour after the game ends.
We keep the result (for example, how many answers matched) and which questions the two of you have already played, so your next game doesn't repeat them. Both go when either account is deleted.

sections.heading: Community
paragraphs: Stamps you post in Our Stamp (a photo and a caption) can be seen by other logged-in Dearlly members, not by the public, and they're not shown on search engines. Your username is shown with each post.
You can delete your own posts at any time; the photo is deleted too. Members can report a post, and we can remove posts that break our rules. Likes are counted to pick the top post of the week.

sections.heading: People who receive a letter
paragraphs: If a sender types in your email address, we use it once to deliver that letter and then delete it. It is never used for marketing and never shared.
Every email has "Stop messages from this sender" and "Never email me again". To honour those, we keep a coded fingerprint of your address, not the address itself.
If you report a letter, we keep the report and your reason so we can review it and spot repeat abuse.

sections.heading: Keeping Dearlly safe
paragraphs: Like every website, our servers see your IP address. We use it briefly to stop spam and attacks (for example, limiting how many login codes can be requested). Server logs are overwritten automatically, and private letter links are removed from them.
When something breaks, an error report is sent to our error-tracking service. Private links, passwords and letter content are removed before it leaves our server.

sections.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: We only use cookies Dearlly needs to work: ones that keep you logged in, one that protects forms from forgery, and a small one that only says "logged in" so pages load fast. No advertising cookies, no tracking across other sites, no analytics.

sections.heading: Who helps us run Dearlly
paragraphs: These companies handle data only to provide their service to us, under their own privacy and security terms:
items: Hostinger: our server, in the European Union.
Cloudflare: website protection, the "are you human" check, private photo storage and our encrypted backups.
Resend: sends our emails.
Sentry: error reports, with personal details removed.
Google: only if you choose "Continue with Google".

sections.heading: How long we keep it
items: Your account and letters: until you delete your account.
"Take back" closes a letter's link straight away; the letter itself is deleted with your account.
Recipient email addresses: deleted as soon as the letter is emailed, or if it is cancelled.
Backups: encrypted, and each one is deleted after 35 days.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask to see the data we hold about you, correct it, move it, object to how we use it, or have it deleted. You can change your name and password and delete your account yourself in Profile. Deleting your account removes your letters and replies straight away.
Write to us and we'll reply within 30 days. If you're not happy with our answer, you can complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (ndpc.gov.ng).

sections.heading: Adults only
paragraphs: Dearlly is for people aged 18 and over. If we learn that an account belongs to someone younger, we delete it.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: When we add something new, like photos or games, we'll update this notice and change the date at the top. If a change matters, we'll tell you by email before it takes effect.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms are the rules for using Dearlly: writing letters and invitations, playing games and posting in Our Stamp. By creating an account or using Dearlly, you agree to them. We've kept them short and in plain English.

sections.heading: Who can use Dearlly
paragraphs: Dearlly is for adults aged 18 and over. When you create an account, you confirm you're 18 or older. We delete accounts that belong to someone younger.
You need an account to send letters, play games and post. People you send letters to don't need one to read them.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: Keep your login to yourself. You're responsible for what's done with your account. If you think someone else has used it, log out of all devices from your profile and tell us.
You can delete your account at any time from your profile. Your letters, photos and posts are deleted with it.

sections.heading: Be kind, be real
paragraphs: Dearlly is for love, friendship and kindness. You agree not to use it to:
items: harass, threaten, bully or frighten anyone;
send or post sexual content, nudity, or anything involving someone under 18;
ask for money, bank details or gifts, run scams, or advertise;
pretend to be someone else, or use secret admirer letters to stalk or pressure anyone;
post photos of other people without their permission;
share hate or violence against anyone for who they are;
break the law, or try to break, overload or get around Dearlly's security.

sections.heading: Letters, invitations and secret admirers
paragraphs: Only send letters to people you know and who would want to hear from you. If someone asks you to stop, stop.
Secret admirer letters hide your name from the person you send them to, but Dearlly always knows who sent them. If people block your secret letters, we can switch the feature off for your account.
Anyone who gets a letter from Dearlly can report it, stop messages from you, or block all Dearlly emails.

sections.heading: Photos and Our Stamp
paragraphs: Only post photos you took or have the right to share, and that everyone in them is happy to have shared. Photos are checked automatically before anyone sees them, and some may be refused.
Posts in Our Stamp are seen by other Dearlly members. You can delete your own posts at any time. We can remove any post that breaks these terms.

sections.heading: Games
paragraphs: Games are for two adults who both want to play. Intense games are deep and flirty but never explicit, and both players have to opt in. Keep the chat respectful.

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: You own what you write and the photos you upload. You give Dearlly permission to store them, show them to the people you send them to (or to members, for posts), and make the copies needed to run the service, such as smaller versions of photos. This permission ends when you delete them, except where we must keep something to deal with a report or the law.
The Dearlly name, design, quotes and game questions belong to Dearlly. You can use the quotes and questions inside Dearlly and share your own letters and results.

sections.heading: When we step in
paragraphs: If you break these terms, we may remove your content, limit features (such as secret admirer letters or posting), or close your account. We act on reports and may contact the authorities when someone's safety is at risk or the law requires it.

sections.heading: Dearlly is provided as it is
paragraphs: We work hard to keep Dearlly running and safe, but we can't promise it will always be available or free of mistakes. Dearlly is free to use today; if we add paid features, we'll say so clearly before you pay for anything.

As far as the law allows, Dearlly isn't responsible for what members write, send or post, or for what happens on dates and trips arranged through invitations. Nothing in these terms takes away rights you have under Nigerian consumer law.

sections.heading: Changes and the law
paragraphs: If we change these terms, we'll update the date at the top, and tell you by email first if a change matters. These terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

safety.title: Staying safe on Dearlly
safety.intro: Dearlly is built for sweet moments, and we want every one of them to feel safe. Here's how we protect you, and how you can protect yourself.

sections.heading: What we do
items: Private letters open only with their link. They never show up on search engines, and the sender can take them back.
Every photo is cleaned of hidden details like your location, and checked for nudity before anyone sees it.
Letters can't contain links or long numbers like bank accounts, which is how many scams start.
Secret admirer letters are limited to 3 a day and can be blocked with one tap. Dearlly always knows who sent them.
Games are played by two adults who both chose to play. Intense games need both to opt in, and are never explicit.
We read and act on every report.

sections.heading: Never send money
paragraphs: Nobody on Dearlly should ever ask you for money, airtime, gift cards, bank details or codes, however sweet their letter. That's a scam. Don't send anything. Report it, and block them.

sections.heading: If a letter or post upsets you
items: Tap "Report this letter" at the bottom of the letter, or ⋯ then Report on a post. The sender won't know it was you.
For a secret admirer letter, tap "Block this secret admirer". It disappears for good.
In any letter email, tap "Stop messages from this sender", or "Never email me again" to stop all Dearlly emails.

sections.heading: Going on a date
paragraphs: Date invitations are lovely, but if you're meeting someone for the first time:
items: meet in a busy public place, like the restaurants and spots in our list;
tell a friend where you're going and who with, and share your live location;
arrange your own way there and back;
trust your feelings: you can always say "Not this time", or leave.

sections.heading: Photos
paragraphs: Only share photos everyone in them is happy to share. Never send private photos to anyone you haven't met, and remember that anything you share online can be copied.

sections.heading: If you're in danger
paragraphs: If you or someone else is in immediate danger in Nigeria, call 112, the national emergency number. Then tell us, so we can act on the account.
